# @rbayuokt/expo-body-vision

> Native body tracking for Expo and React Native: pose rules, rep counting, body-driven targets,
> guided setup, video file analysis and GPU effects. The camera, the pose model, the rules and the
> skeleton overlay all run natively. JavaScript describes what to detect and receives events.

This file is written for coding agents (Claude, Codex, Cursor and similar) helping someone build
with the library. It covers the whole public API, how the pieces fit, recipes, and how to write
custom effects and shaders that plug straight in. Everything here matches the source in this
repository. When something is not listed, it does not exist yet: say so instead of guessing.

## 1. Mental model

- JS describes, native executes, the GPU renders. You pass rules as props. The native engine
  evaluates them on every inference and sends back events (rep counted, pose entered, target hit).
  Camera frames and per-frame joints never cross into JS unless you opt in with `landmarks`.
- One body at a time. 33 BlazePose joints (see `JOINTS`).
- Left and right always mean the person's own left and right, even with the mirrored front camera.
- Default pose backend: MediaPipe on iOS, ML Kit on Android. MediaPipe is also built in on Android.
- Events are batched with backpressure. A busy JS thread never slows tracking or counting.
- Positions in events are view points of the `BodyVisionView`, so overlays placed inside the view
  line up with them directly.

## 2. Install

Needs an Expo development build (not Expo Go). In a bare React Native app, run
`npx install-expo-modules@latest` first.

```bash
npx expo install @rbayuokt/expo-body-vision@latest
npx expo prebuild
```

app.json:

```json
{
  "expo": {
    "plugins": [["@rbayuokt/expo-body-vision", { "cameraPermission": "Used to count your reps." }]]
  }
}
```

Plugin options: `cameraPermission` (iOS usage string), `enableTestInput` (lets `testInput` replace
the camera with recorded frames, for tests and demos, keep it off in shipped apps).

Optional peers, install only what you use:

```bash
npx expo install @shopify/react-native-skia react-native-reanimated  # <BodySetup /> and all effects
npx expo install expo-speech                                          # spoken setup prompts
npx expo install expo-asset                                           # require()'d model or video files
```

Entry points:

| Import | Contains | Needs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `@rbayuokt/expo-body-vision` | View, rules, presets, events hook, video analysis, permissions | nothing extra |
| `@rbayuokt/expo-body-vision/setup` | `<BodySetup />` overlay | Skia, Reanimated |
| `@rbayuokt/expo-body-vision/effects` | Effects, `createImpactEffect`, `useImpactShake` | Skia, Reanimated |

The main entry never imports Skia or Reanimated. Keep it that way in app code too: import effects
only from `/effects`.

## 3. Quick start

```tsx
import { BodyVisionView, squat, useCameraPermissions } from '@rbayuokt/expo-body-vision';
import { useState } from 'react';
import { Button, Text, View } from 'react-native';

export function SquatCounter() {
  const [permission, requestPermission] = useCameraPermissions();
  const [reps, setReps] = useState(0);
  if (!permission?.granted) return <Button title="Allow camera" onPress={requestPermission} />;
  return (
    <View style={{ flex: 1 }}>
      <BodyVisionView
        style={{ flex: 1 }}
        facing="front"
        rules={[squat()]}
        onRep={(e) => setReps(e.count)}
        onRepRejected={(e) => console.log('not counted:', e.reason)}
      />
      <Text style={{ fontSize: 48 }}>{reps}</Text>
    </View>
  );
}
```

## 4. BodyVisionView

Props (all optional):

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `facing` | `'front' \| 'back'` | `front` | `<CameraControls />` or `useCameraControls().flip()` switch it at runtime |
| `torch` | boolean | unset | keeps the torch on where the camera has one. Unset lets `CameraControls` drive it |
| `active` | boolean | true | false stops camera and inference, pauses `video` |
| `resizeMode` | `'cover' \| 'contain'` | `cover` | |
| `performance` | `'auto' \| 'performance' \| 'balanced' \| 'accuracy'` | `auto` | fixed modes run 15, 24, 30 inferences/s, `auto` adapts to latency and heat, `accuracy` also picks the larger model |
| `smoothing` | `'none' \| 'light' \| 'balanced' \| 'stable'` or `{ minCutoff, beta, derivativeCutoff }` | `balanced` | use `none` or `light` for punches and other fast strikes |
| `prediction` | boolean or `{ enabled, maxMs }` | on, 100 ms | extrapolates joints to display time for the overlay |
| `tracking` | `{ minJointConfidence, jointHoldMs, lostAfterMs }` | 0.3, 250, 500 | |
| `rules` | `(RuleDefinition \| TargetDefinition)[]` | none | poses, exercises and targets |
| `skeleton` | `SkeletonStyle` or `false` | lime skeleton | per-bone and per-joint styles, trails |
| `landmarks` | boolean or `{ intervalMs }` | off | opt-in joints to JS, throttled natively (100 ms) |
| `debug` | boolean | false | native stats panel |
| `backend` | string | platform default | `mlkit`, `mediapipe`, or a name you registered |
| `model` | `'lite' \| 'full' \| require('x.task') \| { uri }` | `lite` | MediaPipe model file |
| `experimentalDelegate` | `'cpu' \| 'gpu'` | `cpu` | GPU on Android only |
| `calibration` | `CalibrationResult \| null` | none | reuse a saved calibration |
| `readiness` | boolean or `ReadinessOptions` | off | native positioning checks, results in `onReadiness` |
| `setup` | boolean or `BodySetupOptions` | off | guided setup, see section 7 |
| `testInput` | `ReplayInput \| null` | none | recorded frames instead of the camera, needs `enableTestInput` |
| `video` | uri string, `{ uri }` or `require()` | none | plays a file in place of the camera, live overlay and events |
| `videoLoop` | boolean | false | |

Callbacks: `onCameraReady`, `onBodyDetected`, `onBodyLost`, `onPoseEntered`, `onPoseExited`,
`onExercisePhase`, `onRep`, `onRepRejected`, `onTargetHit`, `onZoneEntered`, `onZoneExited`,
`onPerformanceChange`, `onStats` (about once a second), `onLandmarks`, `onReadiness`,
`onSetupChange`, `onSetupComplete`, `onVideoEnd`, `onError` (a `BodyVisionError` with `.code`).

Key event payloads (every event also has `timestamp` in ms):

- `RepEvent`: `exercise`, `bodyId`, `count`, `durationMs`, and in peak mode `side`
  (`'left' | 'right'`), `joint`, `x`, `y` (view points of the moving joint when it counted).
- `RepRejectedEvent`: `exercise`, `reason` (`'incomplete' | 'too-fast' | 'too-slow' | 'form' | 'lost'`).
- `PoseEnteredEvent`: `pose`, `bodyId`. `PoseExitedEvent` adds `durationMs`.
- `TargetHitEvent`: `target`, `joint`, `bodyId`, `speed` (view short-sides per second), `x`, `y`
  (target center in view points).
- `PerformanceChangeEvent`: `mode`, `inferenceFps`, `reducedEffects`, `thermalLevel`.
- `ReadinessEvent`: `status` (`'noBody' | 'adjusting' | 'ready'`), `issue`, `mirrored`.

Ref (`useRef<BodyVisionViewRef>()`): `calibrate({ durationMs? })` returns `CalibrationResult`,
`resetExercise(id?)`, `restartSetup()`.

Children of `BodyVisionView` render over the camera, in the same coordinate space as event
positions. Put overlays and effects there.

Camera switch and flash: `<CameraControls />` as a child gives a flip button and a flash button
(flash only where `hasTorch`, nothing without a live camera). Props: `style` (position, default
top right), `buttonStyle`, `color`, `activeColor`, `activeIconColor`,
`icons={{ flip, torchOn, torchOff }}`, `labels`. For custom UI, `useCameraControls()` returns
`{ facing, flip, torch, setTorch, hasTorch, available }`. `CameraReadyEvent` has `hasTorch`.

## 5. Rules

### Measurements

```ts
import { above, angle, distance, inclination } from '@rbayuokt/expo-body-vision';

angle('leftShoulder', 'leftElbow', 'leftWrist');   // interior angle at the middle joint, 0..180 degrees
inclination('leftShoulder', 'leftWrist');           // segment angle from horizontal, 0..90 degrees
distance('leftWrist', 'rightWrist');                // in torso lengths (or the calibrated torso length)
above('leftWrist', 'nose');                          // how far a is above b, torso lengths, negative when below
```

Chain `.mirrored()` to also measure the swapped side (better tracked side wins in conditions and
cycle exercises, both sides are watched in peak exercises). Turn a measurement into a condition
with `.atLeast(n)`, `.atMost(n)` or `.between(min, max)`. Joints under `minConfidence` make a
condition unknown, not false.

### Poses

```ts
import { angle, definePose, inclination } from '@rbayuokt/expo-body-vision';

const handsOnHips = definePose({
  id: 'handsOnHips',
  holdMs: 400,          // must hold this long before poseEntered (default 300)
  exitGraceMs: 150,     // may fail this long before poseExited (default 150)
  when: [
    angle('leftShoulder', 'leftElbow', 'leftWrist').between(60, 120),
    angle('rightShoulder', 'rightElbow', 'rightWrist').between(60, 120),
    inclination('leftShoulder', 'leftHip').atLeast(60),
  ],
});
```

### Exercises

```ts
import { angle, defineExercise, inclination } from '@rbayuokt/expo-body-vision';

const curl = defineExercise({
  id: 'curl',
  metric: angle('leftShoulder', 'leftElbow', 'leftWrist').mirrored(),
  top: 150,            // metric is large at the top of the movement
  bottom: 60,          // and small at the bottom
  hysteresis: 10,      // default 10, in the metric's own units
  minRepMs: 600,       // faster reps are rejected as 'too-fast' (default 400)
  maxRepMs: 8000,      // slower ones as 'too-slow'
  lossGraceMs: 400,    // tracking may drop this long mid-rep
  minConfidence: 0.5,
  requires: [inclination('leftShoulder', 'leftHip').mirrored().atLeast(60)], // form checks
});
```

Two counting modes:

- `mode: 'cycle'` (default): `top -> descending -> bottom -> ascending -> top` counts a rep. Turning
  back early, going too fast or too slow, or breaking a `requires` condition emits `onRepRejected`.
  The metric must be large at the top. Use this for squats, push-ups, curls.
- `mode: 'peak'`: counts each rise of at least `top - bottom` that reaches `top`, and re-arms after
  an equal drop. A mirrored metric watches both sides at once, peaks closer than `minRepMs` count
  once, and each rep carries `side`, `joint`, `x`, `y`. Use this for strikes too fast for a full
  cycle to be sampled: punches, kicks, claps. No phase events in this mode.

Important: `hysteresis` defaults to 10, which suits degrees. For distance or `above` metrics
(torso lengths, typically -1.5 to 1.5) set it explicitly, for example `hysteresis: 0.1`, and keep
`top - hysteresis > bottom + hysteresis`.

### Presets

| Preset | What | Key values |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pushUp()` | cycle on elbow angle, mirrored | top 150, bottom 100, minRepMs 500, body within 40 degrees of horizontal |
| `squat()` | cycle on knee angle, mirrored | top 160, bottom 100, minRepMs 400, torso at least 35 degrees upright |
| `punch()` | peak on elbow angle, mirrored | top 110, bottom 80, minRepMs 70, minConfidence 0.2 |
| `tPose()` | pose | arms within 20 degrees of horizontal, elbows at least 150, hold 500 ms |
| `armsUp()` | pose | both wrists above the nose, hold 300 ms |

Every preset takes overrides: `squat({ bottom: 90 })`, `tPose({ id: 'start', holdMs: 1000 })`.
Pushups and squats count best side-on. Punches count best facing the camera with `smoothing="none"`.

### Targets

```ts
import { defineTarget } from '@rbayuokt/expo-body-vision';

const pad = defineTarget({
  id: 'pad',
  x: 0.8, y: 0.3,              // center as fractions of the view
  radius: 0.07,                // fraction of the view's shorter side
  colliders: ['leftWrist', 'rightWrist'],
  minSpeed: 0,                 // view short-sides per second
  cooldownMs: 800,
  mode: 'hit',                 // 'zone' fires onZoneEntered and onZoneExited instead
  style: { hitColor: '#C6FF3D', particles: 16 },
});
```

Hits are swept-circle tested between inference frames, so a fast hand still registers. The
native renderer draws the target and its hit burst. Move a target by changing its `x`, `y`.

## 6. Events inside the view: useBodyVisionEvents

Any component rendered as a child of `BodyVisionView` can listen to every event the callbacks get:

```tsx
import { useBodyVisionEvents } from '@rbayuokt/expo-body-vision';

function RepLogger() {
  useBodyVisionEvents((e) => {
    if (e.type === 'repCompleted') console.log('rep', e.count, e.x, e.y);
  });
  return null;
}
```

Event `type` values: `cameraReady`, `bodyDetected`, `bodyLost`, `poseEntered`, `poseExited`,
`exercisePhase`, `repCompleted`, `repRejected`, `targetHit`, `zoneEntered`, `zoneExited`,
`performanceChanged`, `stats`, `landmarks`, `readiness`, `error`, `videoEnded`. Cast to the typed
event (`e as unknown as RepEvent`) when you need its fields. The hook only works inside a
`BodyVisionView`.

## 7. Guided setup

Walks the user into position, optionally checks a pose, measures their proportions and counts
down, with voice and a built-in overlay or your own UI.

```tsx
import { BodyVisionView, tPose } from '@rbayuokt/expo-body-vision';
import { BodySetup } from '@rbayuokt/expo-body-vision/setup';

<BodyVisionView
  setup={{
    framing: 'fullBody',                      // 'upperBody' | 'floor' (floor wants landscape)
    voice: true,                              // expo-speech, or speak={(text) => ...}
    steps: ['position', { pose: tPose(), prompt: 'Arms out to confirm' }, 'calibrate', { countdown: 3 }],
    prompts: { tooClose: 'Take a step back' },
  }}
  onSetupComplete={(calibration) => save(calibration)}>
  <BodySetup accentColor="#C6FF3D" topInset={100} bottomInset={220} />
</BodyVisionView>
```

For a fully custom look, skip `<BodySetup />` and render from `onSetupChange(state, text)` or
`useBodySetup()` inside the view (`state.phase`, `state.prompt`, `state.progress`,
`state.screenDirection`, `text`, `restart()`). `text` is already resolved from the step prompt, your
`prompts` or the default, so don't map prompt codes yourself. Pass a saved `calibration` prop
later to skip measuring.

Setup first, then counting: pass the rules up front with `startRules: 'afterSetup'`. They stay
inactive until setup is done, the measured calibration applies, and `ref.restartSetup()` pauses
them again. Never remount the view or swap `setup` to `false` to switch from setup to counting.

```tsx
<BodyVisionView
  ref={view}
  setup={{ steps: ['position', { pose: tPose() }, 'calibrate', { countdown: 3 }], startRules: 'afterSetup' }}
  rules={[punch()]}
  smoothing="none"
  onSetupChange={(state, text) => setPrompt(text)}
  onSetupComplete={() => setUnlocked(true)}
/>
```

## 7a. Performance overlay: useBodyVisionStats

`const stats = useBodyVisionStats()` inside any child of `BodyVisionView` returns
`BodyVisionStats | null` about once a second (`renderFps`, `inferenceFps`, `inferenceMs`,
`latencyMs`, `backend`, `delegate`, `thermalLevel`, `bodyVisible`...) and turns native stats on
while mounted. Use it for FPS badges and debug overlays instead of `onStats` plus state.

## 7b. Counting stats: useRepStats

```tsx
import { useRepStats } from '@rbayuokt/expo-body-vision';

const { stats, track, reset } = useRepStats({ comboGapMs: 900, exercises: ['punch'] });
<BodyVisionView rules={[punch()]} {...track} />
// stats: count, left, right, combo, best, streak, missed, lastMiss, lastRepAt
```

Use it instead of writing counters, combo timers or streaks by hand. `track` provides `onRep` and
`onRepRejected`. To also handle reps yourself, call `track.onRep(e)` inside your own `onRep`.
`ComboFever` uses the same combo rule.

## 8. Video files

Analyze every frame of a clip, off the JS thread:

```ts
import { analyzeVideo, squat } from '@rbayuokt/expo-body-vision';

const result = await analyzeVideo(uri, { rules: [squat()], fps: 30, landmarks: false });
const reps = result.events.filter((e) => e.type === 'repCompleted').length;
// result: durationMs, width, height, framesAnalyzed, sourceFps, backend, delegate, averageInferenceMs, events, landmarks?
```

Or play a clip with the live overlay and all callbacks, in place of the camera:

```tsx
<BodyVisionView video={uri} videoLoop rules={[punch()]} smoothing="none" onRep={(e) => setCount(e.count)} />
```

Sources: file or content URI (what `expo-image-picker` returns), a path, or `require('./clip.mp4')`
(needs expo-asset). Portrait phone videos are rotated upright. Android remuxes fragmented MP4s
(common from social apps) before reading. `analyzeVideo` is exhaustive, the `video` prop keeps
pace with playback and may skip frames on slow phones.

## 9. Effects (`@rbayuokt/expo-body-vision/effects`)

GPU effects as children of `BodyVisionView`. Each listens to the view's events, draws with a Skia
runtime shader and animates on the UI thread with Reanimated.

| Component | Fires on | Look |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<ImpactEffect look="anime" />` | peak reps with a position, target hits | speed lines, jagged ink starburst, POW! |
| `look="lightning"` | same | flickering bolts, ZAP! |
| `look="fire"` | same | flame burst with embers, FWOOSH! |
| `look="pixel"` | same | 8-bit pixel ring, rising +1 |
| `look="shatter"` | same | glass cracks and falling shards, CRACK! |
| `look="jojo"` | same | JoJo style purple burst, gold screentone, ink outline, dark speed lines, ORA! |
| `<RepEffect />` | every rep and rejection | count slams in, GOOD! or PERFECT!, red crack with the reason |
| `<RepEffect look="levelUp" every={5} />` | every N reps | golden ring sweep, LEVEL 2 |
| `<ComboFever from={5} />` | reps chained within `gapMs` | edge flames that grow, x10 COMBO |
| `<PoseAura poses={['tpose']} />` | while a pose holds | energy aura, grows with hold time |
| `<SetupConfetti />` | setup done, or `trigger` changing | confetti, READY! |

```tsx
import { BodyVisionView, punch, squat } from '@rbayuokt/expo-body-vision';
import { ComboFever, ImpactEffect, RepEffect, useImpactShake } from '@rbayuokt/expo-body-vision/effects';
import Animated from 'react-native-reanimated';

export function Arena() {
  const shake = useImpactShake();
  return (
    <Animated.View style={[{ flex: 1 }, shake.style]}>
      <BodyVisionView style={{ flex: 1 }} rules={[punch(), squat()]} smoothing="none">
        <ImpactEffect look="lightning" onImpact={shake.shake} />
        <RepEffect exercises={['squat']} />
        <ComboFever from={5} />
      </BodyVisionView>
    </Animated.View>
  );
}
```

Props:

- `ImpactEffect`: `look`, `on` (`'reps' | 'hits' | 'both'`), `sources` (exercise or target ids),
  `colors` (`{ left, right }`), `words` (array or `false`), `wordStyle`, `size` (radius, default
  120), `durationMs`, `speedLines`, `flash`, `ring`, `onImpact(impact)`, `level`.
- `RepEffect`: `look` (`'slam' | 'levelUp'`), `exercises`, `every`, `perfectAfter` (default 3),
  `labels` (`good`, `perfect` and each rejection reason, `''` to stay quiet), `levelLabel`,
  `colors` (`good`, `perfect`, `rejected`, `level`), `showCount`, `textStyle`, `size`,
  `durationMs`, `onPlay`, `level`.
- `ComboFever`: `from`, `full`, `gapMs` (default 900), `exercises`, `color`, `banner` (function or
  `false`), `bannerStyle`, `bannerTop` (position from the top, e.g. below a header, default
  `'11%'`), `onCombo`, `level`.
- `PoseAura`: `poses`, `growMs` (default 3000), `color`, `level`.
- `SetupConfetti`: `colors` (five), `label` (or `false`), `labelStyle`, `durationMs`, `trigger`, `level`.
- `useImpactShake(strength = 9)`: `{ style, shake }`. Put `style` on an `Animated.View` around the
  `BodyVisionView`.

Levels (every effect): `minimal` (hits drawn in a small box, no words or extra layers, at most two
at a time, other effects show text only), `balanced` (three hits, drawn near the hit, words and
speed lines, no flash), `max` (everything over the whole view), `auto` (default, balanced and
dropping to minimal while `performance="auto"` reports `reducedEffects`). Explicit layer props
(`speedLines`, `flash`, `ring`, `words`) override the level. Suggest `level="minimal"` when a user
reports lag on a low-end phone.

Where hits land: an `ImpactEffect` needs a position. Peak-mode reps (`punch()` or any
`mode: 'peak'` exercise) and target hits carry one. Cycle-mode reps (squats, push-ups) do not, use
`RepEffect` for those.

## 10. Custom effects

Three levels of control, pick the lowest one that does the job.

### 10a. Restyle a built-in

```tsx
<ImpactEffect look="anime" words={['JAB!', 'CROSS!']} colors={{ left: '#FFC23D', right: '#FF6B4A' }} size={90} speedLines={false} />
```

### 10b. createImpactEffect: your own shader, the library does the rest

```ts
import { createImpactEffect } from '@rbayuokt/expo-body-vision/effects';

const Ripple = createImpactEffect({
  shader: RIPPLE_SKSL,                 // see the contract below
  words: ['SPLASH!'],                  // or false
  colors: { left: '#3DD6FF', right: '#3DD6FF' },
  size: 120,
  durationMs: 600,
  risingWords: false,                  // true floats words up like a score pickup
});

// Use it exactly like ImpactEffect (same props, except `look`):
<Ripple on="reps" sources={['punch']} level="balanced" />
```

Call `createImpactEffect` once at module scope, never inside a component body: it compiles the
shader. A shader that fails to compile throws `BodyVisionError('INVALID_CONFIG')`.

Shader contract. SkSL with `half4 main(float2 p)` where `p` is the pixel in view points. Declare
only the uniforms you use, any subset of:

| Uniform | Type | Value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `center` | `float2` | where the hit landed, view points |
| `progress` | `float` | 0 at the hit to 1 at the end, eased out |
| `radius` | `float` | the `size` prop |
| `tint` | `float3` | side color, 0..1 per channel |
| `seed` | `float` | random 0..1 per hit, use it to vary shapes |
| `useLines` | `float` | 1 or 0, from `speedLines` or the level |
| `useFlash` | `float` | 1 or 0, from `flash` or the level |
| `useRing` | `float` | 1 or 0, from `ring` or the level |

Rules for writing SkSL that works here:

- Return premultiplied color: `return half4(half3(color * alpha), half(alpha));`. Returning an
  un-premultiplied color makes edges glow white or look dirty.
- Fade to alpha 0 by `progress` 1. The effect is removed at the end, anything still visible pops.
- Use float literals (`1.0`, not `1`) and fixed-count loops (`for (int i = 0; i < 8; i++)`).
- `out`, `in`, `inout` are reserved words, don't use them as variable names.
- There is no texture of the camera. Effects draw over it and cannot warp or sample the video.
- Everything outside the drawing box is clipped: at `balanced` the box is about 2.6 x `radius`
  around the hit, at `minimal` 1.35 x. Keep the core of the effect within `radius` so it survives
  cheaper levels. Full-view parts like speed lines only show at `max`.
- Cost is per pixel per frame. Prefer a few `smoothstep` and `length` calls over deep noise, keep
  loops short, and let `useLines` and friends switch off expensive layers.
- Hash helper that varies per hit:
  `float hash(float n) { return fract(sin(n * 127.1 + seed * 311.7) * 43758.5453); }`

Example shaders that compile and follow the contract:

```glsl
// RIPPLE: a double ring that expands and fades.
uniform float2 center;
uniform float progress;
uniform float radius;
uniform float3 tint;

half4 main(float2 p) {
  float d = length(p - center);
  float fade = 1.0 - progress;
  float r1 = radius * progress;
  float r2 = radius * progress * 0.6;
  float ring = smoothstep(5.0, 0.0, abs(d - r1)) + 0.6 * smoothstep(4.0, 0.0, abs(d - r2));
  float a = clamp(ring * fade, 0.0, 1.0);
  return half4(half3(tint * a), half(a));
}
```

```glsl
// HEART_BURST: small hearts fly out from the hit and fade.
uniform float2 center;
uniform float progress;
uniform float radius;
uniform float3 tint;
uniform float seed;

float hash(float n) { return fract(sin(n * 127.1 + seed * 311.7) * 43758.5453); }

// 1 inside the heart curve (x^2 + y^2 - 1)^3 - x^2 y^3 < 0, soft at the edge. y points up.
float heart(float2 q) {
  q.y = -q.y * 1.1 + 0.25;
  float r = q.x * q.x + q.y * q.y - 1.0;
  float f = r * r * r - q.x * q.x * q.y * q.y * q.y;
  return smoothstep(0.05, -0.05, f);
}

half4 main(float2 p) {
  float a = 0.0;
  for (int i = 0; i < 8; i++) {
    float fi = float(i);
    float ang = (fi + hash(fi) * 0.5) / 8.0 * 6.2831853;
    float dist = radius * progress * (0.6 + 0.6 * hash(fi + 3.0));
    float2 pos = center + float2(cos(ang), sin(ang)) * dist;
    float s = radius * 0.12 * (1.0 - progress * 0.5);
    a = max(a, heart((p - pos) / s));
  }
  a *= 1.0 - progress;
  return half4(half3(tint * a), half(a));
}
```

```glsl
// SLASH: a bright diagonal cut through the hit that opens and fades, with a flash.
uniform float2 center;
uniform float progress;
uniform float radius;
uniform float3 tint;
uniform float seed;
uniform float useFlash;

half4 main(float2 p) {
  float2 v = p - center;
  float ang = 0.6 + seed * 1.8;
  float2 dir = float2(cos(ang), sin(ang));
  float along = dot(v, dir);
  float across = dot(v, float2(-dir.y, dir.x));
  float len = radius * 1.6 * smoothstep(0.0, 0.25, progress);
  float width = mix(10.0, 1.0, progress);
  float cut = smoothstep(width, 0.0, abs(across)) * step(abs(along), len);
  float fade = 1.0 - smoothstep(0.4, 1.0, progress);
  float flash = useFlash * (1.0 - smoothstep(0.0, 0.1, progress)) * 0.2 * step(length(v), radius * 2.0);
  float a = clamp(cut * fade + flash, 0.0, 1.0);
  float3 c = mix(tint, float3(1.0), cut * 0.7);
  return half4(half3(c * a), half(a));
}
```

Wire one up:

```ts
const Slash = createImpactEffect({ shader: SLASH_SKSL, words: ['SLASH!'], durationMs: 450 });
```

Check a shader before running the app: Skia's web build (`canvaskit-wasm`, installed with
`@shopify/react-native-skia`) compiles the same SkSL in Node.

```js
const CanvasKitInit = require('canvaskit-wasm/bin/canvaskit.js');
CanvasKitInit().then((CK) => {
  let error = '';
  const effect = CK.RuntimeEffect.Make(source, (e) => (error = e));
  console.log(effect ? 'ok' : error);
});
```

This repository runs that check for every built-in shader in `src/__tests__/shaders.test.ts`.

### 10c. Fully custom: useBodyVisionEvents plus Skia or Reanimated

For effects that are not a hit (a HUD pulse, a screen tint while a pose holds, particle trails),
listen to events and draw whatever you like. This one flashes the screen edge red on a rejected
rep and green on a counted one:

```tsx
import { useBodyVisionEvents, type RepEvent } from '@rbayuokt/expo-body-vision';
import { StyleSheet } from 'react-native';
import Animated, { useAnimatedStyle, useSharedValue, withSequence, withTiming } from 'react-native-reanimated';

export function RepGlow() {
  const good = useSharedValue(0);
  const bad = useSharedValue(0);
  useBodyVisionEvents((e) => {
    if (e.type === 'repCompleted') good.set(withSequence(withTiming(1, { duration: 80 }), withTiming(0, { duration: 500 })));
    if (e.type === 'repRejected') bad.set(withSequence(withTiming(1, { duration: 80 }), withTiming(0, { duration: 700 })));
  });
  const goodStyle = useAnimatedStyle(() => ({ opacity: good.value }));
  const badStyle = useAnimatedStyle(() => ({ opacity: bad.value }));
  return (
    <>
      <Animated.View pointerEvents="none" style={[StyleSheet.absoluteFill, styles.edge, { borderColor: '#C6FF3D' }, goodStyle]} />
      <Animated.View pointerEvents="none" style={[StyleSheet.absoluteFill, styles.edge, { borderColor: '#FF4A4A' }, badStyle]} />
    </>
  );
}

const styles = StyleSheet.create({ edge: { borderWidth: 10 } });

// <BodyVisionView rules={[squat()]}><RepGlow /></BodyVisionView>
```

For shader-based custom effects outside the hit contract, use Skia directly: `Skia.RuntimeEffect.Make`
once at module scope, a `<Canvas style={StyleSheet.absoluteFill} pointerEvents="none">`, a `<Rect>`
with `<Shader source={effect} uniforms={derived} />`, and Reanimated shared values for time and
progress (`useDerivedValue`, `useClock` from Skia). Mount the canvas only while the effect is
visible, an idle full-view shader still costs every frame.

Do not stream `landmarks` to JS to place per-frame effects. Positions already arrive on the events
that matter (peak reps, target hits). If an effect truly needs a joint every frame, it belongs in
native code.

## 11. Custom pose backends (native)

Register your own detector and select it by name. Swift:

```swift
import ExpoBodyVision

final class MyBackend: BodyVisionPoseBackend {
  let delegateName = "cpu"
  func detect(_ buffer: CMSampleBuffer, timestampMs: Int, into result: BodyVisionPoseResult) throws {
    // upright, unmirrored 32BGRA buffer, report normalized 0..1 coordinates
    result.setJoint("leftWrist", x: 0.4, y: 0.6, confidence: 0.9)
  }
}
BodyVisionBackends.register("my-model") { options in MyBackend() }
```

Kotlin:

```kotlin
class MyBackend : BodyVisionPoseBackend {
  override val delegateName = "cpu"
  override fun detect(frame: BodyVisionFrame, timestampMs: Long, result: BodyVisionPoseResult) {
    // frame.bitmap() is unrotated: report coordinates in it (the library rotates them by
    // frame.rotationDegrees) or set result.upright = true if your SDK returns upright ones
    result.setJoint("leftWrist", 0.4, 0.6, confidence = 0.9)
  }
  override fun close() {}
}
BodyVisionBackends.register("my-model") { options -> MyBackend() }
```

Then `<BodyVisionView backend="my-model" />`. `getCapabilities().backends` lists what is
registered. The same backend serves `analyzeVideo`. A custom `.task` MediaPipe model needs no
native code: `model={require('./pose_landmarker_heavy.task')}` with `task` added to Metro's
`assetExts`.

## 12. Testing without a camera

```tsx
import { BodyVisionView, parseBodySequence, pushUp } from '@rbayuokt/expo-body-vision';

<BodyVisionView testInput={parseBodySequence(csv, { loop: false })} rules={[pushUp()]} onRep={onRep} />
```

Requires the plugin's `enableTestInput: true`. The CSV format is the one in the repo's
`fixtures/`. For a real person on video use `analyzeVideo` or the `video` prop instead.

## 13. Errors

`onError` and rejected promises carry `BodyVisionError` with a stable `code`:
`CAMERA_PERMISSION_DENIED`, `CAMERA_UNAVAILABLE`, `CAMERA_INTERRUPTED`, `MODEL_LOAD_FAILED`,
`INFERENCE_FAILED`, `GPU_UNAVAILABLE`, `INVALID_CONFIG`, `INVALID_RULE` (with `.path`, for example
`rules[1].conditions[0].joints`), `TEST_INPUT_DISABLED`, `VIDEO_READ_FAILED`, `CALIBRATION_FAILED`,
`NOT_MOUNTED`, `UNSUPPORTED_PLATFORM`. Rules are validated in JS where they are written and again
natively.

## 14. Recipes

### Boxing trainer with jab and cross counts and effects

```tsx
import { BodyVisionView, punch, type RepEvent } from '@rbayuokt/expo-body-vision';
import { ComboFever, ImpactEffect, useImpactShake } from '@rbayuokt/expo-body-vision/effects';
import { useState } from 'react';
import Animated from 'react-native-reanimated';

export function Boxing() {
  const shake = useImpactShake();
  const [jabs, setJabs] = useState(0);
  const [crosses, setCrosses] = useState(0);
  const onRep = (e: RepEvent) => (e.side === 'left' ? setJabs((n) => n + 1) : setCrosses((n) => n + 1));
  return (
    <Animated.View style={[{ flex: 1 }, shake.style]}>
      <BodyVisionView style={{ flex: 1 }} rules={[punch()]} smoothing="none" onRep={onRep}>
        <ImpactEffect look="anime" onImpact={shake.shake} />
        <ComboFever from={5} />
      </BodyVisionView>
    </Animated.View>
  );
}
```

Jab is the left hand for an orthodox stance and the right for southpaw. Ten punches in one second
at 30 fps is past what motion-blurred frames show, normal pace counts well.

### Jumping jacks (a custom cycle exercise on an `above` metric)

```ts
import { above, defineExercise } from '@rbayuokt/expo-body-vision';

const jumpingJack = defineExercise({
  id: 'jumpingJack',
  metric: above('leftWrist', 'nose').mirrored(), // arms up: positive, arms down: about -1
  top: 0.1,
  bottom: -0.6,
  hysteresis: 0.1,  // torso lengths, not the degree default
  minRepMs: 400,
});
```

### JoJo's Bizarre Adventure style rush (custom effect)

This look is built in, `<ImpactEffect look="jojo" />` gives it to you with no shader code. The
recipe shows the same look made with `createImpactEffect`, as a template for variants (other
colors, other words, another screentone): a jagged purple burst with gold manga screentone, an
ink outline, dark speed lines, ORA! words and an ORA ORA ORA combo banner.

```glsl
uniform float2 center;
uniform float progress;
uniform float radius;
uniform float3 tint;
uniform float seed;
uniform float useLines;

float hash(float n) { return fract(sin(n * 127.1 + seed * 311.7) * 43758.5453); }

half4 main(float2 p) {
  float2 v = p - center;
  float d = length(v);
  float a01 = atan(v.y, v.x) / 6.2831853 + 0.5;
  float pop = smoothstep(0.0, 0.12, progress);
  float fade = 1.0 - smoothstep(0.45, 1.0, progress);

  // Jagged burst with long uneven spikes.
  float k = a01 * 16.0;
  float spike = 1.0 - abs(fract(k) * 2.0 - 1.0);
  float starR = radius * (0.4 + 0.75 * spike * mix(0.35, 1.0, hash(floor(k)))) * pop;
  float inside = smoothstep(starR, starR - 2.0, d);
  float ink = smoothstep(starR + 7.0, starR + 4.0, d) - inside;

  // Manga screentone: dots that grow toward the center of the burst.
  float cell = 7.0;
  float2 g = fract(p / cell) - 0.5;
  float dotR = mix(0.12, 0.48, 1.0 - clamp(d / (starR + 1.0), 0.0, 1.0));
  float tone = smoothstep(dotR + 0.06, dotR - 0.06, length(g));
  float3 gold = float3(1.0, 0.82, 0.24);
  float3 fill = mix(tint, gold, tone);
  fill = mix(fill, float3(1.0), smoothstep(radius * 0.25, 0.0, d));

  // Dark dramatic speed lines around the hit.
  float lk = a01 * 90.0;
  float on = step(0.45, hash(floor(lk) + 40.0));
  float line = on * smoothstep(0.35, 0.0, abs(fract(lk) - 0.5));
  float from = radius * (1.1 + 0.9 * hash(floor(lk) + 9.0));
  float lines = useLines * line * smoothstep(from, from + 60.0, d) * smoothstep(radius * 3.2, radius * 2.2, d)
              * (1.0 - smoothstep(0.0, 0.55, progress)) * 0.85;

  float3 c = float3(0.12, 0.02, 0.18) * lines;
  float a = lines;
  c = mix(c, float3(0.02), ink * fade); a = max(a, ink * fade);
  c = mix(c, fill, inside * fade); a = max(a, inside * fade);
  return half4(half3(c * a), half(a));
}
```

```tsx
import { BodyVisionView, punch } from '@rbayuokt/expo-body-vision';
import { ComboFever, createImpactEffect, useImpactShake } from '@rbayuokt/expo-body-vision/effects';
import Animated from 'react-native-reanimated';

const JOJO_SKSL = `...the shader above...`;

const JojoEffect = createImpactEffect({
  shader: JOJO_SKSL,
  words: ['ORA!', 'ORA ORA!', 'ドドド'],
  colors: { left: '#B14CFF', right: '#B14CFF' },
  size: 110,
  durationMs: 520,
});

const oraBanner = (combo: number) => Array(Math.min(combo, 4)).fill('ORA').join(' ') + '!';

export function OraRush() {
  const shake = useImpactShake();
  return (
    <Animated.View style={[{ flex: 1 }, shake.style]}>
      <BodyVisionView style={{ flex: 1 }} rules={[punch()]} smoothing="none">
        <JojoEffect onImpact={shake.shake} />
        <ComboFever from={5} color="#B14CFF" banner={oraBanner} />
      </BodyVisionView>
    </Animated.View>
  );
}
```

### Squat coach with feedback effects

```tsx
import { BodyVisionView, squat } from '@rbayuokt/expo-body-vision';
import { RepEffect } from '@rbayuokt/expo-body-vision/effects';

<BodyVisionView rules={[squat()]}>
  <RepEffect labels={{ incomplete: 'GO DEEPER', 'too-fast': 'SLOW DOWN' }} />
  <RepEffect look="levelUp" every={10} levelLabel={(n) => `SET ${n}`} />
</BodyVisionView>
```

### Reaction game with targets

```tsx
import { BodyVisionView, defineTarget } from '@rbayuokt/expo-body-vision';
import { ImpactEffect } from '@rbayuokt/expo-body-vision/effects';
import { useState } from 'react';

const SPOTS = [[0.2, 0.3], [0.8, 0.3], [0.5, 0.2]];

export function Reaction() {
  const [i, setI] = useState(0);
  const [x, y] = SPOTS[i];
  return (
    <BodyVisionView
      style={{ flex: 1 }}
      rules={[defineTarget({ id: 'pad', x, y, radius: 0.08, cooldownMs: 300 })]}
      onTargetHit={() => setI((n) => (n + 1) % SPOTS.length)}>
      <ImpactEffect look="shatter" on="hits" />
    </BodyVisionView>
  );
}
```

### Count reps in an uploaded video

```ts
import { analyzeVideo, pushUp } from '@rbayuokt/expo-body-vision';
import * as ImagePicker from 'expo-image-picker';

const picked = await ImagePicker.launchImageLibraryAsync({ mediaTypes: ['videos'] });
if (!picked.canceled) {
  const result = await analyzeVideo(picked.assets[0].uri, { rules: [pushUp()] });
  const counted = result.events.filter((e) => e.type === 'repCompleted').length;
  const rejected = result.events.filter((e) => e.type === 'repRejected');
}
```

## 15. Advice for agents

- Start from presets and only write custom rules when a preset can't be tuned with overrides.
- Setup before counting: `setup={{ ..., startRules: 'afterSetup' }}` plus `rules`, never a remount.
- Counts, combos and streaks come from `useRepStats`, don't hand-roll them.
- Put effects and overlays inside `BodyVisionView`. Hooks like `useBodyVisionEvents` and
  `useBodySetup` return nothing outside it.
- Fast movements: `smoothing="none"` (or `light`) and `mode: 'peak'`.
- Distance and `above` metrics: always set `hysteresis` in torso units.
- Left and right are the person's, not the screen's.
- Effects need a dev build with Skia and Reanimated installed. Import them only from `/effects`.
- Use Reanimated for animation, not React Native's `Animated`.
- Performance numbers depend on the phone. Suggest `level="minimal"` and `performance="auto"`
  for low-end devices instead of promising a frame rate.
- Test logic without a camera through `testInput` recordings or `analyzeVideo` on a real clip.
